source.dropped: Ticket #, Customer Complaint free text, Zip code and 'Filing on Behalf of Someone' are not included. The complaint text is used only to derive 'cat' and 'pc'.

rules.d: Days since 2015-04-01 (0..90) using the corrected date. Calendar date = 2015-04-01 + d days.
rules.date: The sheet's Date_month_year column has day and month swapped whenever the real day is 1-12 (the source dd-mm text was read as mm-dd). Evidence: in the stored data every date with day<=12 has day 4, 5 or 6 only, so Jan-Mar and Jul-Dec contain only days 4-6; after swapping day/month for those rows, all 2,224 dates fall in 1 Apr-30 Jun 2015 and all 91 days of that range are present. 572 rows were swapped. To reproduce the owner's Power BI month axis (which uses the stored dates, Jan-Dec), use the stored month = (day-of-month <= 12 ? day-of-month : month) of the corrected date.
rules.h: Hour 0-23 taken from the Time column (complaint received time).
rules.resolved: Solved or Closed count as resolved (Resolution % = (Solved+Closed)/total = 76.75%, matching the dashboard). 'Open Cases' on the dashboard counts Status = Open only (363); Pending (154) is neither resolved nor counted as open there.
rules.state: 'District Of Columbia' (16 rows) merged into 'District of Columbia'. Otherwise state and city names are as given.
rules.category: APPROXIMATE keyword grouping derived by the portfolio data script, not by the owner. Lower-cased complaint text is tested against these regex keywords group by group, first match wins; nothing matched = Other: Data caps & usage: data cap, \bcap(s|ped)?\b, usage, overage, \bgb\b, data limit, metered, data plan, threshold, consumption | Speed & throttling: speed, slow, throttl, mbps, bandwidth | Billing & pricing: bill, charg, \bfees?\b, pric, refund, credit, payment, \bpay, cost, \brates?\b, promo, money, collection, expensive | Outages & connectivity: outage, connect, \bdown\b, drop, intermittent, no internet, no service, signal, modem, equipment, router, not working, reliab, loss of, \blost\b | Unfair / deceptive practices: unfair, decept, fraud, false, mislead, bait, \blie, lying, monopol, contract, scam, unauthori, practice, block, neutral | Customer service & support: customer service, customer care, \brude\b, representative, \breps?\b, technician, \btech\b, appointment, support, poor service, bad service, terrible, horrible, help, cancel, install, lack of service, failure, run around, nightmare. About 29% stay in Other, mostly generic titles such as 'Comcast', 'Comcast Internet', 'Comcast Service'.
rules.pbiCategory: pc = a RECONSTRUCTION of the owner's Power BI 'Complaint_Type' column (its DAX is inside the compressed .pbix model and could not be read). Case-sensitive substring test on the original text, first match wins: 'speed' -> Internet Speed, 'bill' -> Billing, 'service' -> service, 'outage' -> Network, else Other. It reproduces every Complaint_Type number visible in the three dashboard screenshots, but it is an inference, not the confirmed formula. Use it only to mirror the original dashboard; 'cat' is the more useful grouping.
